results.title: FDA approves selpercatinib for RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer | FDA
results.content: On June 12, 2024, the Food and Drug Administration granted traditional approval to selpercatinib (Retevmo, Eli Lilly and Company) for adult and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with advanced or metastatic *RET* fusion-positive thyroid cancer who require systemic therapy and who are radioactive iodine-refractory (if radioactive iodine is appropriate). Efficacy was evaluated in LIBRETTO-001 (NCT03157128), a multicenter, open-label, muti-cohort clinical trial in 65 patients with *RET* fusion-positive thyroid cancer who were radioactive iodine (RAI)-refractory (if RAI was an appropriate treatment option) and were systemic therapy naïve and patients who were previously treated, in separate cohorts. Supportive evidence included ORR and DOR data from 10 pediatric and young adult patients with *RET* fusion-positive thyroid cancer treated in Study LIBRETTO-121 (J2G-OX-JZJJ; NCT03899792), an international, single-arm, multi-cohort clinical trial of selpercatinib in pediatric and young adult patients with advanced *RET*-altered solid tumors. For assistance with single-patient INDs for investigational oncology products, healthcare professionals may contact OCE’s Project Facilitate at 240-402-0004 or email OncProjectFacilitate@fda.hhs.gov.

results.title: Oncology Drugs Fast-Tracked by the FDA in February 2026
results.content: On Feb. 4, [Oncolytics Biotech Inc. announced](https://uk.finance.yahoo.com/news/oncolytics-biotech-receives-fda-fast-135000618.html) that the FDA granted fast track designation to pelareorep, an [immunotherapy](/category/immunotherapy), in combination with [bevacizumab](https://www.oncologynewscentral.com/drugs/monograph/78648-304008/bevacizumab-intravenous) (Avastin) and FOLFIRI (leucovorin, fluorouracil, and irinotecan), for the treatment of patients with KRAS-mutated, microsatellite-stable metastatic [colorectal cancer](/category/colorectal-cancer) in the second-line setting. On Feb. 19, [Pilatus Biosciences Inc. announced](https://www.pilatusbio.com/latest-news/pilatus-biosciences-receives-fda-fast-track-designation-for-metabolic-checkpoint-inhibitor-plt012-in-hepatocellular-carcinoma) that the FDA granted fast track designation to PLT012, an anti-CD36 monoclonal antibody, for the treatment of patients with HCC. On Feb. 23, [Artios Pharma Limited announced](https://www.artios.com/press-release/artios-receives-u-s-fda-fast-track-designation-for-dna-polymerase-theta-pol%ce%b8-inhibitor-art6043-for-treatment-of-gbrca-mutated-her2-negative-breast-cancer/) that the FDA granted fast track designation to ART6043, a DNA polymerase theta inhibitor, in combination with [olaparib](https://www.oncologynewscentral.com/drugs/monograph/167487-315030/olaparib-oral) (Lynparza), a PARP inhibitor, for the treatment of adult patients with BRCA-mutated, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic [breast cancer](/category/breast-cancer) who have not received prior PARP therapy. On Feb. 24, [Aktis Oncology Inc. announced](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/aktis-oncology-receives-u-fda-130000308.html) that the FDA granted fast track designation to AKY-1189, a nectin-4 miniprotein radioconjugate, for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma (UC) who progressed on or after prior systemic therapies.

results.title: FDA approves selpercatinib for medullary thyroid cancer with a RET mutation | FDA
results.content: # FDA approves selpercatinib for medullary thyroid cancer with a RET mutation. On September 27, 2024, the Food and Drug Administration granted traditional approval to selpercatinib (Retevmo, Eli Lilly and Company) for adult and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with advanced or metastatic medullary thyroid cancer (MTC) with a RET mutation, as detected by an FDA-approved test, who require systemic therapy. Selpercatinib received accelerated approval for this indication for patients 12 years of age and older in 2020. On May 29, 2024, the FDA granted accelerated approval for this indication to pediatric patients 2 years of age and older. The recommended selpercatinib dose for pediatric patients 2 to less than 12 years of age is based on body surface area and is based on weight for patients 12 years of age and older. For assistance with single-patient INDs for investigational oncology products, healthcare professionals may contact OCE’s Project Facilitate at 240-402-0004 or email OncProjectFacilitate@fda.hhs.gov.
